title: Rename a file in the Thunar file manager

capabilities.why: Thunar, and xdotool, which setup places its window with.

setup.why: Make the run's folder holding only the file to rename.
Open Thunar on the run's folder.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && echo $$ > /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}-thunar.pid && exec thunar /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}

setup.why: Wait for Thunar's window (20 s at most), make it fill the screen, put the pointer on it and activate it: a window manager gives the keys to the window activated, and with none they go to the window under the pointer.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); w=$(timeout 20 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --class thunar | head -n1); [ -n "$w" ] || { echo no Thunar window in 20 s >&2; exit 1; }; eval $(xdotool getdisplaygeometry --shell); xdotool windowmove $w 0 0 windowsize $w $WIDTH $HEIGHT; xdotool mousemove $((WIDTH / 2)) $((HEIGHT / 2)); xdotool windowactivate $w 2>/dev/null; sleep 1

instruction: In the file manager, rename the file {{f.old}}-{{nonce}}.txt in /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} to {{f.new}}-{{nonce}}.txt.

checks.why: The folder lists exactly one file, named {{f.new}}-{{nonce}}.txt: the old name is gone and no copy was made. After setup it lists {{f.old}}-{{nonce}}.txt, so an agent that does nothing fails.
The renamed file holds the text setup wrote, so it is the same file, not a new empty one with the name.

teardown.why: Close the run's Thunar (by the pid setup kept beside the folder: a desktop may have other Thunar windows open) and delete the run's folder.

argv: for f in /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}-*.pid; do [ -f "$f" ] && kill -9 "$(cat "$f")" 2>/dev/null; done; rm -f /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}-*.pid; rm -rf /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}; true

oracle.why: Select the folder's one file (Ctrl+A) and open Rename (F2): its dialog opens centred over Thunar, under the pointer. Select the whole name in its field (Ctrl+A), type the new name and press Enter.
